ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points A, B, and C are all on circle $O$. When $\angle OAC = 40^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let's select any point D on the major arc AB, and connect AD and CD.\\
Since OA=OC, $\angle$OAC=40$^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle$OAC=$\angle$OCA=40$^\circ$,\\
which implies $\angle$AOC=180$^\circ$-40$^\circ$-40$^\circ$=100$^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle$D=$\frac{1}{2}$$\angle$AOC=50$^\circ$,\\
Since quadrilateral ABCD is circumscribed around $\odot$O,\\
it follows that $\angle$D+$\angle$B=180$^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle$B=180$^\circ$-50$^\circ$=\boxed{130^\circ},

A is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and B is on the lower minor arc between A and C. Because OA and OC are both radii, OA = OC, triangle AOC is an isosceles triangle, so ∠OCA = ∠OAC = 40°. Therefore the central angle ∠AOC = 180° - 40° - 40° = 100°. According to the inscribed angle theorem, ∠B = 1/2 × 260° = 130°.
